title: Expiration time validated
description:
## v1.2.1
  - `jwt_encode_*()` and `jwt_decode_*()` now can validate expiration time based on `duration` parameter, default `NULL` for back compatibility.
  - `jwt_decode_*()` now rise `warning("Not checking expiration time")` if `exp` not specified
  - All tests passing with `supressWarnings` when needed
  - Tests entry adapted to suggested packages with `requireNamespace()`
  - New unit tests for `validate_exp()`
  - Documentation adapted
  - `linterR` recommendations included

## NOTE
 Default `duration` value initially was fixed to 12h, but then failed on stored values, finally given the huge difference in tokens lifetime, `NULL` was used. Future versions could create a warning or a hard error if parameter is not supplied. Checking _immortal_ tokens could be accomplished with _far-future_ `duration` values on `jwt_decode_*()`.

title: Allow headers to override typ in jwt_encode_sig
description:

Closes #15, as discussed there.

title: Check the 'exp' field and error if token has expired
Include jwt_split in export (issue #4)
description:
Currently, the `jwt_split` function is not available externally. However, the function is very useful if users want to read the payload of a JWT they did not create themselves. The pull request is based on issue #4 .

The pull requests includes:
* the updated roxygen comments for export in `jwt.R`
* a short example section in `jwt.R`
* updates of the automated files (NAMESPACE & RD)

Alternatively, I propose to define a function that returns only the payload of a given JWT.
